stated_limits: gitleaks is optional in the hook: when it is absent there is one WARNING and the commit proceeds. CI's secret-scan job is the mandatory scan. On a public repo that job is DETECTION, not prevention, and it is not a required check until the owner adds it in branch protection.
Without gitleaks, M2 stays open for shapes outside the six regex branches (e.g. py_compile echoes a GitHub token on a Python syntax-error line) (TB7, review 13).

A textconv command or an external diff (diff.external, GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF, a diff.<driver>.command) that FAILS refuses the commit with 'could not read the staged diff'; the base hook passed silently (review correction 1, TBF3).

When gitleaks 8.30.1 logs an ERR line and exits 0 (e.g. a textconv driver that writes to stderr while working), the commit is refused with 'run gitleaks git --pre-commit --staged by hand' (TBF1, fail-closed). The hook never prints gitleaks' stderr, because an ERR line can quote git's stderr.

The TBF1 test is the substring ' ERR ' on gitleaks' --no-color log at log level error, the same test as the CI step. A future gitleaks that changes its level text or ignores --no-color is guarded only by its exit code and report.
An awk that passes the one-line probe but dies while reading the staged-diff file lets steps 4 and 4a pass on an empty stream. The .env value pass still refuses when a .env exists.

Content at an ALLOWLISTED asset path that carries the right magic bytes (UTF-16, NUL or attribute-binary) is regex-scanned only as far as --text exposes ASCII runs, and never for UTF-16. A secret inside an allowlisted image is never read (TB14).

Attribute-forced text (an untracked .gitattributes, or .git/info/attributes with `diff`) and UTF-16 with no NUL in its first 8,000 bytes pass the binary refusal. The regex checks still read the --text view (TBF4, #317).

The binary refusal covers PDF, archives, office files, databases and executables, and images or fonts outside the TB3 rows (e.g. landing/ OG images, tests/fixtures images, test_images/*.jpg, a UTF-16 .ps1). Each stays refused until its path is allowlisted in .githooks/pre-commit in its own commit (TB3, adversary A5).

A work-tree .gitleaksignore is refused only when gitleaks is installed; with gitleaks absent, a committed one is caught by the CI guard (TBG3). The hook's gitleaks always reads HEAD's .gitleaks.toml or a default-only file, never the working tree's (TBF2). `--no-verify` bypasses every check (TB14).
CI reads .gitleaks.toml from the range base, so an allowlist change must land in its own PR first.
